To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new approach for model‐independent personalized dosing of anticancer drugs that is based on Bayesian data assimilation and reinforcement learning and has the potential to substantially improve the efficacy and the safety of anticancer drug therapies.

we developed a novel approach to model‐informed personalized dosing that is capable of integrating multiple patient‐specific information and that allows for an improved prediction of treatment outcomes and a reduction in the incidence of dose‐limiting toxicities.

we propose three novel approaches based on Bayesian data assimilation and/or reinforcement learning for model‐inforced precision dosing using therapeutic drug/biometric monitoring to control neutropena, the major dose-limiting side effect in anti-cancer chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for MIPD and the identification of patient factors that drive the dosing decisions.
the development of a novel MIPD framework for personalized anticancer chemotherapy based on RL and DA.
